origin.description: Convert each string to Unicode Normalization Form KC.
origin.details: NFKC is compatibility decomposition followed by canonical composition. The fi ligature becomes fi. U+FDFA expands to 18 code points. A missing value stays missing and an empty string stays empty.
origin.value: A character vector of the same length as str, in UTF-8.
origin.example:
got <- stri_trans_nfkc("ﬁ")
cat(paste0("stri_trans_nfkc of the fi ligature returns ", paste(sprintf("U+%04X", utf8ToInt(got)), collapse = " "), ".
"))

translation.description: Convert each string to Unicode Normalization Form KC.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A string, NA, or a list or tuple of those.

translation.details: unicodedata.normalize with NFKC matches this form. NA stays NA and an empty string stays empty.
translation.value: The normalized string, or a list of strings when str is a list or tuple.
translation.example:
from stringi.normalize import stri_trans_nfkc
got = stri_trans_nfkc("ﬁ")
print("stri_trans_nfkc of the fi ligature returns " + " ".join(f"U+{ord(char):04X}" for char in got) + ".")
